transcript.text: my belling cooker keeps burnin stuff 1 day then next day its undercookd on same temp. been like it a cuple months. thermastat??

To answer your question directly: on an electronic oven (digital), the part that regulates temperature is usually the temperature sensor and control board, not a mechanical thermostat. On a mechanical dial model, it would be the thermostat. The symptom of alternating between burning and undercooking suggests the oven isn't maintaining a steady temperature. Before we look at parts, please check two things:
1. Are you using the same setting (e.g., Fan Bake) for both tests?
2. Is the fan actually running when it's supposed to be heating? If it's a fan oven and the fan is off, food will burn on top but stay raw inside. To help me guide you further: does your cooker have a digital display with buttons, or rotary dials?

its got rotary knobs not a digital display. i think the fan is spinning, i can hear it. not allways same setting tho, sometimes i put stuff in straight away without waiting for it to heat up. i mostly do roasts and lasagne and cakes

Since it's a rotary-knob model, the part that regulates temperature is indeed the mechanical thermostat (often linked with a capillary tube). The alternating burning and undercooking suggests this thermostat is drifting—it thinks one temperature when it's actually another. To check if the heating element itself is weak or broken: set the oven to 180°C Fan Bake and leave it for 5 minutes. Then look through the door at the ring-shaped heater behind the fan; does it glow bright orange/red all around? If you can't see clearly, just tell me how hot the inside feels after that time.

ok i put it on 180 for 5 mins but i cant really see the heater thru the door, its a bit dark and the glass is greasy lol. i dont have a thermometer either so cant tell u how hot it is exactly. what else could i check?

Since you can't see the element clearly, we need to check how accurately the oven maintains its heat. The alternating burning and undercooking on a rotary model suggests the mechanical thermostat inside the control knob is drifting—it's not switching the heating off at the right time. Preheat to 180°C Fan Bake as normal. Once the knob clicks off (indicating it thinks it has reached temperature), wait another 2 minutes then read the thermometer. Is the actual temperature significantly higher than 180°C (e.g., over 200°C) or lower? This will confirm if the thermostat is regulating correctly.
i dont have a thermometer so cant tell u the actual temp. the neon light goes off after about 10 mins sometimes but other times it seems to stay on for ages. is that any help?

The fact that the neon light stays on for ages sometimes suggests the thermostat isn't switching off when it should—this 'drifting' causes the oven to overshoot temperature and burn food. We need to check if the heating element itself is failing (which would cause undercooking) or just dirty/loose. Please isolate the cooker at the mains, then remove the rear inner panel to inspect the fan element for cracks or loose connections. If it looks fine, the thermostat inside the rotary knob is probably the part that needs replacing.
hmm i dont really want to take panels off, i havnt got any tools and im not an electrician lol. is there anything easier i can check? the knob is a bit wobbly if that helps

The wobbly knob is a useful clue: if the internal mechanism of that rotary switch is worn or loose, it can cause the thermostat to drift between temperatures, which explains why one day it burns and the next it undercooks. There isn't an easy owner-safe check that can definitively prove this without replacing the part. The most likely cause is a worn mechanical thermostat inside the control knob assembly. As this requires removing panels and working near live electrical connections, I recommend calling a qualified appliance engineer to check the thermostat or the entire control module for you.

candidates: Incorrect oven setting or user error (e.g., fan vs. conventional) (medium)
